issue: The same structure has two node IDs at one point, which disconnects the network there. 118 pairs of node IDs lie within 0.5 m. In 12 of them one node has no recorded invert. At six of these a dead-end network joins the catchment once the pair is merged: SL7044 at 8Z7020 (118 nodes upstream), DN481 at DN925 (28), WT2366 at WT81 (14), DN7504b at DN806 (11), WT2020b at WT3020 (2), and OS7500 at OS351 (1). OS1437 and OS7035, on the 1,200 mm trunk into the plant, were another such pair (D24).
resolution: Node IDs within 0.5 m are merged unless their recorded inverts differ by more than 1 m or a pipe already joins them, keeping the maintenance-hole ID (107 pairs merged). A missing invert does not prevent a merge, so 11 of the 12 pairs with one are merged, including all six above; the twelfth, WT1507 and WT433, is already joined by a pipe. Every pair is listed in node_merges.csv, and those touching the catchment that are not merged in the build log (hydraulics/greenway/).

issue: Pipes with no recorded length (43 city-wide).
resolution: Length computed from the pipe's geometry, in the London projected coordinate system (EPSG:2958).

issue: Nodes with no invert recorded in any layer (83 city-wide), including the 1,200 mm trunk OS7035 to OS2272 into the plant.
resolution: Interpolated by length between the nearest recorded nodes up- and downstream (45 nodes), or, at the head of a run, set at a slope of 0.005 from the node downstream (147 nodes). Each fill is flagged in the model input and listed in the build log. The City gives the inverts of maintenance holes OS2270, OS2271, and OS2272 on that trunk (233.945, 233.582, and 233.116 m), which are used instead [@london2026answers]. The last pipe, 283433 from OS2272 to the plant, continues the trunk's slope (0.0012) to 232.683 m and drops 8.3 m into the low-level wet well, as the south inlet pipe 131179 does.

issue: Pipe and drop-structure inverts outside the plausible 150–350 m range (45 city-wide), e.g. pipe 142170 at 25,089.0 m (probably 250.89 m), which, uncorrected, blocks the Wonderland trunk.
resolution: Treated as missing and filled as in D04. Each is flagged in the model input and listed in the build log. The City confirms that pipe 142170's downstream invert is 250.89 m, which is used, and that the drop-structure values of pipes 99538, 132529, and 138550 are not elevations: their recorded pipe inverts are right [@london2026answers].

issue: Built sanitary pipes in the catchment with no size (10).
resolution: Size copied from the pipe downstream (7), or taken as circular where a height and width are recorded but no diameter (3). The City gives 200 mm for pipe 319968 (WM1727 to WM847, otherwise copied as 250 mm) and suggests 200 mm for the private pipe 360080 (OK913 to OK7013, otherwise copied as 1,050 mm), which are used [@london2026answers].

issue: Pipe shape code S, or blank.
resolution: The City confirms that S means square [@london2026answers], which is modelled as a closed rectangle with equal sides; no pipe in the catchment has it. A blank code (6 pipes) is taken as circular.

issue: Two 900 mm pipes on Ridout St N (OBJECTID 328065 and 328066) are still listed as Proposed after construction. Without them about 590 maintenance holes, including the Victoria Hospital area, do not reach the plant.
resolution: Taken as built. The City confirms that both pipes are in service [@london2026answers].

issue: Pipe 117908 (300 mm, OS1079 to OS1135) climbs 1.7 m and carries about 1,400 upstream maintenance holes.
resolution: Kept as recorded. The City confirms its size and inverts: the pipe is an inverted siphon [@london2026answers]. With the D08 correction it does not flood.

issue: Abandoned 750 mm pipe whose IDs are the word Abandoned enters the plant node.
resolution: Excluded with all non-built pipes. The City confirms that the pipe is out of service [@london2026answers].

issue: Overflow pipes create splits and dead ends that carry no dry-weather flow (215 removed).
resolution: Excluded from the dry-weather network.

issue: Dingman Creek P.S. (WO6001): its 600 mm force main 112216 (2005) to WO893 and a 1.2 m gravity outlet (2011) form a loop, through the 900 mm sewers WO893 to WO622 and back to the station.
resolution: Force main 112216 removed: the City confirms that it is abandoned, replaced by the 750 mm force main 299074 (D13), and that the 1.2 m outlet is a gravity bypass [@london2026answers]. The station pumps by 299074, and the bypass is removed with it (D13).

issue: Pipe 299074 (750 mm force main, 2020, no inverts) is recorded as WT7026 to WT7025, the Wonderland Rd main, but it is drawn from 113 m from the Dingman Creek P.S. along Dingman Dr, over the route of the abandoned 1968 Dingman force main, and continues as pipe 299075 (750 mm, 2020) to WT2366, on the 1,200 mm Wharncliffe Rd trunk 11 m below where the Wonderland Rd main discharges. A description of the station, rebuilt in 2010, says it discharges either to Greenway by a 750 mm force main on Dingman Dr or by the 1,500 mm gravity sewer on Dingman Dr to the Wonderland Rd P.S., and sends high flows to the Dingman Creek Storage Facility.
resolution: The City confirms that pipe 299074 is the current Dingman Creek P.S. force main [@london2026answers]. Its ends are taken as the station and WO7026, the start of pipe 299075, so that the station pumps along Dingman Dr to WT2366 on the Wharncliffe Rd trunk. Its line is drawn back to the station along the first 142.6 m of the 1968 main, whose route it follows, and that stretch is added to its length. The station's 1.2 m gravity outlet to WO864 (pipe 141130, 2011) is a bypass and is removed, so the station's flow no longer passes the Wonderland Rd P.S.

issue: Pond Mills P.S.: the 350 mm force main ends at the top of the gravity sewer that drains back to the station.
resolution: Kept; the closing links carry no flow and are removed before transport. The City confirms that the force main discharges at PM171, that the 675 mm sewer east from PM171 is the main flow path, and that the 200 mm sewer to the south leaves PM171 1 m higher [@london2026answers].

issue: Three pipes start and end at the same node: 144575 (CV364, 0.1 m), 144194 (WT2265, 0.3 m), and 279038 (DN897, 0.2 m). Pipe 279038 is a stub inside maintenance hole DN897 on Fullarton St (2016). The outlet 279040 is recorded as leaving DN897 but is drawn from a point 0.16 m from the maintenance hole, and the stub bridges the two; its inverts (245.696 to 245.318 m) are those of the neighbouring pipes 279039 and 279041. Flow arrives by 279041 and leaves by 279040 without it. It reaches the catchment only since DN481 and DN925 are merged (D01).
resolution: Removed.

issue: A force main (135454) leaves node SH93 and climbs 20 m, but no pumping station is recorded there.
resolution: An ideal pump is added at SH93. The City confirms that SH93 is the Sunninghill P.S., rated at 50 L/s with two duty pumps and one standby [@london2026answers].

issue: Station inverts above the pipes arriving at them; Medway P.S. took its force main's invert, 3.66 m too high.
resolution: Station inverts set to the lowest arriving pipe (Medway, Victoria St, W12A).

issue: No pump capacities, wet-well sizes, or operating levels in the open data.
resolution: Ideal pumps that pass their inflow without storage; force mains as full conduits with the City's Hazen–Williams coefficient by diameter [@london2025dsrm4]. The City gives each station's control mode and firm capacity [@london2026answers]. The ideal pumps are kept, since the modelled dry-weather peaks are within the firm capacities. Wet-well sizes and operating levels remain unknown.

issue: Force main from Berkshire Village P.S. ends at WT1560, 30 m from the plant, with no pipe onward.
resolution: Superseded by D28: the force main is joined to the plant. The City confirms that the Berkshire Village P.S. discharges to the plant's main headworks [@london2026answers].

issue: Arva, A.E. Duffield, Wellington Heights, Coves Mobile Home Park, and 69 Waterloo St have pumping stations but no upstream pipes in the open data.
resolution: External inflows omitted. The City has no flow data for these stations; Arva, A.E. Duffield, Wellington Heights, and Coves Mobile Home Park are private stations outside the City's control, and 69 Waterloo St is a small station serving one house that the City advises is not worth modelling [@london2026answers]. The 69 Waterloo St station and its force main (142943) are therefore left out of the model. The City's 2025 report on Arva servicing gives a 30 L/s servicing agreement for the Arva P.S.

issue: Maintenance holes with no lid elevation, one at or below the invert, or one far from the ground.
resolution: The recorded rims are compared with a 1 m bare-earth lidar model of the ground. Missing rims, and recorded rims more than 1 m below or 3 m above the ground plus the median offset, are set to the ground plus that offset, each flagged in data_gaps.csv. Junctions still without a rim take the median recorded depth.

issue: Private drain connection counts missing or implausible (more than 100 on a pipe; three pipes carry about 26,000).
resolution: Imputed from the FSA's connections per metre of pipe.

issue: The 1,200 mm Horton St trunk (OS1048 to OS1501, OS7014, OS1051, OS1052, and OS1437), which carries the downtown flow from the King St and Becher St trunk, is broken in the data at both ends. Pipe 131564 (OS1050 to OS7014) is recorded from OS1050 but drawn from maintenance hole OS1501, 104 m from OS1050, where pipe 136667 from OS1048 ends at the same invert (235.337 m). Pipe 128103 (OS1052 to OS1437) ends at the point where the 1,200 mm OS2272 trunk into the plant starts from OS7035, with no pipe recorded between OS1437 and OS7035. Read as recorded, the downtown flow takes 450 and 300 mm pipes from OS1394 to OS1079 and floods there (D09), and OS2272 carries almost no flow.
resolution: Both ends are taken to be at the structures they are drawn at: pipe 131564 starts at OS1501 and pipe 128103 ends at OS7035, so the downtown flow reaches the plant through OS2272. Asked of the City. With OS2272 carrying flow, the three inlets identify two contrasts rather than one (see the robustness checks of the paper).

issue: Zone outlets used as candidate sampling sites must be structures that can be sampled. The other-nodes layer also holds tees, caps, chambers on force mains, and points where a pipe's slope, material, or installation date changes [@london2026answers]; an earlier zone outlet, WT7027, is an air release chamber on the Wonderland Rd force main. City sampling maintenance holes must have no drop structure [@london2024dsrm3], and 256 maintenance holes in the catchment have no drop record.
resolution: Cuts are chosen only at pumping stations and at maintenance holes without a drop structure. Where there is no drop record, a maintenance hole has a drop if a sewer arrives 0.6 m or more above its outlet, the City's threshold for a drop [@london2024dsrm3], and it is left out if those inverts are missing. The drop record decides where there is one: at WT1420 and WT2191, a 200 mm sewer arrives 5.9 m and 0.66 m above the outlet with no drop recorded.

issue: Node IDs reused for different structures far apart (42 city-wide, 23 in the catchment). Pipes of a 2017 subdivision (Heardcreek Trail, Red Pine Cross, and Tokala Trail) carry 16 IDs of a 2015 subdivision (FH204 to FH215, FH218, FH219, FH248, and FH7003) (Buroak Dr, Eagletrace Dr, Melsetter Way, and Coates Lane) 450 to 1,465 m away, although the maintenance-hole layer lists those structures under their own IDs (FH231 to FH245 and FH440). Read by ID, the two subdivisions are joined, which makes 8 false loops.
resolution: Pipe ends with one ID more than 50 m apart are split into one node per structure (e.g. FH207a and FH207b). A node with no maintenance-hole point takes its invert and type from its pipes, and an end that lies on another structure is then merged into it as in D01. Each split is listed in hydraulics/greenway/reused_ids.csv and the build log. Pipe 144019, recorded FH212 to FH213, is drawn and graded the other way, so its node IDs are swapped; without the swap, FH213b has no outlet and the branch above it does not reach the plant.

issue: A 13 m, 200 mm force main (126757) leaves node OS6007, a maintenance hole whose rim is recorded at its invert, and climbs 2.6 m to the 450 mm sewer at OS950, but no pumping station is recorded there. Without a pump, the sewage from the four nodes upstream floods at OS6007.
resolution: An ideal pump is added at OS6007, taken as a lift station.

issue: The Berkshire Village P.S. force main (112045, 600 mm, 1,164 m, from WT7021) ends at WT1560, 25 m from the low-level station WT6011 at the plant, and the data do not join them, so its network (1,082 nodes, about 21,600 people) is not in the WT6011 catchment. No station is recorded at WT7021. The plant's total daily flow, in the City's monthly operating summaries and in the monitoring data, includes the flow of every inlet.
resolution: WT1560 is joined to WT6011 by a 25 m link added to the data (pipe 900001), so that WT6011 carries the combined influent that the plant flow and the composites measure. An ideal pump at WT7021 sends the flow along the force main. The City confirms that the Berkshire Village P.S. discharges to the main headworks, and that the one inlet metered separately in the operating summaries is the south inlet, the 1,350 mm sewer through WT2203, not this force main [@london2026answers].

issue: Medway P.S. (WM6002) has two force mains: 600 mm along Windermere Rd (138271, 2000) toward the network ending at AD7010, and 400 mm (139920, 1972) toward Greenway. The City's 2025 report on Arva servicing says the station can direct flows to either the Greenway or the Adelaide plant, but not which it does in dry weather. About 38,400 people drain to the station.
resolution: All of the station's flow is sent to Greenway by the 400 mm main; the 600 mm main is left out. The City confirms that the station sends its flow mainly to Greenway, up to about 350 to 400 L/s, and diverts the rest to Adelaide [@london2026answers]; the modelled dry-weather flow at the station stays below that.

issue: Pipe 207149 (WT2359 to 5C7016) is recorded as rectangular with no height or width.
resolution: Taken as 300 mm round, the size of 5C7016's other outlet (207151).

issue: 38 pipes leave the catchment from nodes inside it. 15 start at summit maintenance holes, where two runs fall away from one structure on the ridge between catchments. 20 are gravity pipes from nodes with area upstream: most end at a single node where the data stop, likely relief or overflow connections, and a few lead toward the networks ending at OX8000, AD7010, and VH8000 (likely the Oxford, Adelaide, and Vauxhall plants). A 21st, from DN7009 to the downtown network ending at DN457, is inside the catchment once that network is joined (D32). 3 are force mains: Medway's (D29) and two short ones from the Dingman Creek stations to sanitary outfalls (WO6001 to WO5001, 300 mm, and WO6012 to WO5002, 700 mm).
resolution: Left out: the catchment keeps only pipes with both ends in it, the people on them are not counted, and in dry weather the flow is taken to go down the node's other outlet. Each is listed by swmmbuilder's boundary report. The two Dingman Creek force mains to outfalls are taken as emergency overflows, with no dry-weather flow; asked of the City. The DN457 network is joined to the catchment (D32).

issue: The 790 mm downtown trunk on Ridout St (pipe 129376, 1897) is recorded from DN454 to DN457 but drawn to maintenance hole DN921, at almost the same invert (237.76 m, against 237.78 m). DN921 starts the 1,050 mm trunk built in 2023 that runs down Ridout St and King St into the Greenway catchment, and no pipe is recorded as arriving at it. DN457 is in none of the node layers, and the only other pipe recorded to it, the 250 mm pipe 115350 from DN456 (1991), is drawn to a point 12 m from DN921. A 990 mm pipe from DN921 to DN758 (348485, 1916) is marked Removed. Without a connection, the downtown network (619 nodes, about 14,100 people) drains nowhere. The 1,050 mm trunk matches the 200 m, 1,050 mm trenchless sewer on Ridout St N from King St to Fullarton St in the City's tender for Downtown Loop Phase 2 (2021).
resolution: DN457, placed at the drawn end of pipe 115350, is joined to DN921 by a 12 m, 790 mm link added to the data (pipe 900002) at a slope of 0.001 from DN457's invert, so both pipes recorded to DN457 drain to DN921. Asked of the City.

issue: Pipe 133300 (900 mm, 25 m) joins OS1048, the head of the 1,200 mm Horton St trunk (D24), to OS1424, where Z02's outlet pipe 136335 arrives. Both maintenance holes have the same invert (235.906 m), so the pipe is almost flat (a fall of 0.025 m toward OS1424), and the data do not show which way it flows.
resolution: Kept as recorded. In the model the water level at OS1424 stands above OS1048, so the pipe flows from OS1424 to OS1048, against its drawn direction (about 15 L/s on average), and about a third of Z02's sewage reaches the plant through the Horton St trunk and OS2272 rather than through WT1420. The transport model follows the modelled flows; the population count on the network graph follows the drawn direction. To be asked of the City with D24.

issue: On dry days, the share of the plant's flow metered at the south (Westminster) inlet (the 1,350 mm sewer through WT2203) rose from about 28 % in 2022 to 40 to 46 % from the spring of 2023. The City suggests that a large industrial water user that started up in 2023 is the likely cause [@london2026answers].
resolution: Not modelled: no flow records for a single user are available, so industrial zones keep the uniform loading per hectare. The model is calibrated to the plant's total flow, so its split between the two inlets, and with it the representation of zones at WT2203, may differ from the plant's.
